subject: Quantaflow: custom SLA addendum — service tolerance matrix & order-form clauses
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@quantaflow.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantaflow Legal <legal@quantaflow.io>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custom SLA addendum request — Quantaflow MSA/SOW attachments

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — Quantaflow is moving quickly and procurement asked me to surface a few must-haves so we can get an order form and PO over the line. We're aiming to sign an MSA + SOW and need a short addendum that clarifies availability and latency commitments for our production inference workloads. High level asks: 

- Global availability target: 99.95% monthly (we can discuss regional carve-outs).
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for text-generation API in our primary region (us-west).
- Service credits: a graduated credit schedule by severity/impact window; prefer credits that apply per-day rather than per-incident.
- Evidence: sample telemetry extract and retention window (telemetry + audit logs for 90 days).
- Escalation: contact/response SLAs for Sev1 incidents and a defined failover behavior if a region degrades.

Attached is a short PDF that summarizes Quantaflow procurement's redlines and what our legal team will need for routing the PO. Can your team propose order-form language we can feed into our procurement system? Also note we may ask for a short pilot period (60 days) with slightly relaxed credits while we validate traffic patterns.

Requested next steps: please confirm feasibility, share draft addendum/order-form language, and indicate any evidence you need from our side. We are hoping to route DocuSign by the week of Jul 19.

Attachments: [Attachment: quantaflow-sla-request.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Liam Chen
Head of Procurement, Quantaflow
liam.chen@quantaflow.io
+1 415-555-0132

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@quantaflow.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 12:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Custom SLA addendum request — Quantaflow MSA/SOW attachments

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list and the PDF. I appreciate the timeline. I've looped in Marcus (serving/runtime) and Kimberly (legal/procurement) to scope the addendum and the evidence requests. Quick acknowledgements and clarifications from our side: 

- 99.95% monthly availability: generally achievable, but we need to confirm whether you require a hard guarantee for the entire global footprint or only for the primary region (us-west). Regional fallback behavior affects credits and the order-form wording.
- Latency p95 250ms: we can meet that for standard prompt sizes (<1024 tokens) on our Dedicated/Hosted premium tier; for longer sequences or larger context we'll need to document thresholds.
- Credits: we typically structure a graduated credit schedule tied to monthly availability buckets; Marcus will propose a tolerance matrix that maps to order-form language.
- Evidence: Kimberly, can you confirm whether Quantaflow's procurement needs raw telemetry extracts or an RPM-style evidence package (csv + runbook snippets)? We normally provide an evidence matrix and a sample telemetry extract for the retention period requested.

I'll turn this over to Marcus and Kimberly to draft language and a short implementation checklist (failover paths, on-call routing, telemetry samples). Can you also confirm whether the pilot (60 days) needs different SLA language or if we just mark it as "validation" in the order form?

Best,
Sofia
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Custom SLA addendum request — service tolerance matrix draft

Hi all — jumping in with technical constraints and a proposed mapping for the order-form language. Below is a concise implementation/acceptance checklist and the tolerance matrix I recommend for production traffic.

Proposed acceptance checklist (we will produce short artifacts for each):
- Targeted region: us-west primary; cross-region failover to us-east within 3 minutes for control-plane and up to 15 minutes for warmed KV caches (documented as part of the addendum).
- Supported prompt envelope: up to 1,024 tokens end-to-end for guaranteed p95 <= 250ms on Redwood Hosted Premium. Longer requests will be measured and billed separately; order form should reference the envelope.
- Evidence package: "uptime-evidence-matrix.xlsx" (attached) + sample telemetry extract (JSONL) and runbook excerpt. Retention: 90 days for telemetry, 12 months for audit logs.
- Credits schedule (proposed):
  * Monthly availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.90% <= availability < 99.95%: 5% of monthly fees
  * 99.00% <= availability < 99.90%: 15% of monthly fees
  * availability < 99.00%: 30% of monthly fees plus optional remediation plan
- Degraded-mode fallback: automatic routing to a lower-cost model variant with notice to customer; credits only if automatic fallback does not restore defined throughput within 30 minutes.

Notes on wording for order form (short snippets we can paste into your SOW):
- "Service Commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Service Availability of 99.95% measured on a monthly basis for Customer traffic in the Primary Region as defined in the Order Form."
- "Evidence: Redwood will provide uplink telemetry samples and an evidence matrix within 5 business days of a written request. Telemetry retention: 90 days. Audit logs retention: 12 months."
- "Failover: Redwood may route customer traffic to an alternate region or model variant in response to capacity constraints or regional outages; customer credits apply only if automatic fallback does not restore service to contractual levels within 30 minutes and following the remediation plan."

Attached: [Attachment: redwood-uptime-evidence-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

If that all looks reasonable, Kimberly can translate the snippets into legal redlines and I'll prepare the telemetry sample and the evidence matrix. Sofia — I can draft a short implementation timeline and a limited pilot clause for the 60-day validation period (suggest we mark pilot traffic under a "validation" flag with waived credits, unless an SLA breach occurs due to Redwood negligence).

Marcus
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Sofia / Marcus / Kimberly — thanks, all. The matrix and snippets are helpful and align with procurement's expectations. Two quick asks before we hand this to our legal team: 

1) Kimberly — can you produce a tracked redline we can attach to our MSA (we'll route DocuSign once redlines are accepted).
2) Sofia — can you share the telemetry sample and the evidence matrix (the attached PO requires a sample evidence extract that matches the first 30 days of traffic).

I've attached our PO stub for finance (Quantaflow-PO-12345). If possible we'd like a DocuSign-ready package by Jul 19 so finance can process payment the week after signing. If any of the suggested credit buckets are non-starters for Redwood, flag them and we can discuss alternatives (e.g., longer remediation windows, cap on annual credits).

Liam
